name: Fish Tail Lodge
summary: A long-established lakeside hotel on the far shore of Phewa Lake near its southern end, reached by a short raft ferry across the water. Gardens, quiet and the reflection of Machhapuchhre are the draw, with Lakeside a few minutes away.
body: Fish Tail Lodge sits across a narrow stretch of water from the Phewa dam end of Lakeside, and guests cross on a flat raft pulled along a rope, a small ritual that separates the hotel from the street. The low buildings are set among lawns and trees by the water, and on clear mornings Machhapuchhre, the Fishtail peak that gives the lodge its name, appears above the far shore.

This is a hotel for staying put: breakfast by the lake, a book in the garden, an evening drink as the light goes off the mountains. Lakeside's cafes, boat stands and shops are a short ferry and walk away, and the Peace Pagoda trail and Davis Falls are close. Ask for a room facing the lake and the range.
why: The only well-known hotel reached by ferry across Phewa
Gardens on the water with Machhapuchhre views
Quiet nights yet minutes from Lakeside

faqs.q: How do you get to Fish Tail Lodge in Pokhara?
faqs.a: Fish Tail Lodge is on the far side of a narrow channel at the southern end of Phewa Lake, near the dam end of Lakeside. Guests cross on a rope-pulled raft ferry from the landing near the road, taking a few minutes. Staff help with luggage. Taxis from the airport drop you at the ferry landing.

faqs.q: Is Fish Tail Lodge close to Lakeside?
faqs.a: Yes. Once across the ferry, Lakeside's southern end with restaurants, shops and boat stands is a few minutes' walk, and central Lakeside is 15–20 minutes on foot or a short taxi. The ferry makes the hotel feel more secluded than its distance suggests. Check ferry hours if you plan late evenings out.

faqs.q: Can you see the mountains from Fish Tail Lodge?
faqs.a: On clear days, especially mornings from October to April, Machhapuchhre and the Annapurna range are visible above the hills across Phewa Lake, often reflected in the water. Lake-facing rooms and the gardens have the best views. In the monsoon, June to September, cloud usually hides the peaks.

name: Temple Tree Resort & Spa
summary: A garden resort of stone and timber buildings in Lakeside, Pokhara, a short walk from Phewa Lake, with a spa and a calm courtyard feel. A comfortable base for the lake and the town, and a good place to recover after a trek.
body: Temple Tree is set back from the busy Lakeside road behind walls, around gardens with traditional-style buildings of stone, brick and carved wood. Step through the gate and the scooters and shop music fade. Rooms open onto the gardens, and the spa, as the name promises, is part of the experience.

Its position is practical: Phewa's boat stands, the cafes of Lakeside and the start of the Sarangkot and Peace Pagoda walks are all within easy reach on foot. It suits travellers who want comfort and some calm without leaving town, and trekkers who want a hot shower and a massage after a week on the trails. Book early for October and November.
why: Garden setting behind walls in central Lakeside
Walking distance to Phewa and Lakeside cafes

faqs.q: Where is Temple Tree Resort in Pokhara?
faqs.a: Temple Tree Resort & Spa is in Lakeside, Pokhara, a short walk from Phewa Lake and the main strip of restaurants and shops. It is about 15–20 minutes by taxi from Pokhara International Airport and the Tourist Bus Park. Its walled gardens make it quieter than its central location suggests.

faqs.q: Is Temple Tree Resort good after a trek?
faqs.a: Yes. It is a popular choice for trekkers returning from Poon Hill, Mardi Himal or Annapurna Base Camp, with comfortable rooms, gardens and a spa for massages. Being in Lakeside, it is close to trekking agencies, permit offices and restaurants. Many agencies can store excess luggage here while you trek; confirm in advance.

faqs.q: Is Temple Tree Resort suitable for families?
faqs.a: It works well for families who want comfort and a central location, with gardens for children and easy walks to the lake for boating. Ask about room configurations when booking, as family rooms may be limited. Lakeside traffic means children should be supervised on the road outside.

name: The Pavilions Himalayas
image_query: The Pavilions Himalayas The Farm Pokhara villa
summary: A villa resort in a forested valley outside Pokhara, also known as The Farm, built around sustainability: renewable energy, rainwater harvesting and food from its own organic farm, with a spa, yoga studio and a salt-treated pool facing the Annapurnas.
body: The Pavilions Himalayas sits in farmland and forest away from Lakeside, with private villas of stone walls, Nepali textiles and fireplaces, each with its own terrace. The Annapurna range forms the backdrop on clear days, and the evenings are quiet: no traffic, only birds, the river and the occasional buffalo bell from the village.

The resort was founded on a sustainability idea that shapes daily life here. It runs on renewable energy, harvests rainwater, makes its own biodegradable toiletries and supplies its restaurant from its organic farm. It employs locally and supports a nearby school. The wellness centre includes a spa, sauna and yoga studio, and the outdoor pool is treated with Himalayan salt.
why: Private villas in a quiet valley outside the city
Food from its own organic farm
Spa, yoga and a salt-treated pool with mountain views

faqs.q: How far is The Pavilions Himalayas from Pokhara Lakeside?
faqs.a: The resort lies in a rural valley outside Pokhara, roughly 30–40 minutes' drive from Lakeside depending on the road, and similar from the airport. It feels far from the city, which is the point. The resort can arrange transfers; most guests use them rather than local taxis.

Sustainability is central to it. The resort powers its operation with renewable energy, harvests rainwater, makes biodegradable toiletries, sources ingredients from its own organic farm, employs local staff and supports a nearby school. It is often described as one of Pokhara's leading eco-luxury stays.

faqs.q: Is The Pavilions Himalayas good for a honeymoon?
faqs.a: Yes. Private villas with fireplaces and terraces, a spa, yoga and farm-to-table dining in a quiet valley make it one of the most popular couples' stays near Pokhara. It pairs well with a few nights at Lakeside or a short trek. Book well ahead for October, November and spring.

name: Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge
image_query: Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge ridge Annapurna
summary: A small hilltop lodge on a ridge above the Pokhara valley, about 30 minutes from the city, with stone cottages, verandas facing the Annapurna range, an infinity pool and gardens rich in butterflies. Known for its long commitment to responsible tourism.
body: Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge is built along a ridge above the valley, its stone-and-slate cottages arranged so that each room has a veranda looking north to Machhapuchhre, the Annapurnas and, on clear days, Dhaulagiri and Manaslu. It has been open since the late 1990s and was one of the pioneers of eco-tourism in Nepal, with natural gardens that attract many butterfly species.

Days here are slow: sunrise from your veranda, walks along the ridge to surrounding villages, an afternoon by the infinity pool, dinner as the lights of Pokhara come on below. The lodge suits travellers who want peace and views rather than Lakeside's cafes. Recent guests praise the setting and staff; ask about any refurbishment work when you book.
why: Every room has a veranda facing the Annapurnas
Quiet ridge setting with village walks

faqs.q: Where is Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge?
faqs.a: The lodge sits on a ridge above the Pokhara valley, about 30 minutes' drive from the city and airport. Its ridge-top position gives wide views of the Annapurna range. The lodge arranges transfers, which is easier than finding the last section by taxi. It is a base for slow stays rather than for Lakeside nightlife.

faqs.q: What can you do at Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge?
faqs.a: Guests watch sunrise over the Annapurnas from their verandas, walk to nearby villages and along the ridge, swim in the infinity pool, birdwatch and look for butterflies in the natural gardens, and arrange day trips to Pokhara, Begnas Lake or Sarangkot. It is a place for rest rather than activities.

faqs.q: Is Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge good for older travellers?
faqs.a: It suits older travellers looking for quiet, views and good service, with transfers arranged and no need to navigate Lakeside. The ridge setting means some paths and steps between cottages and the main building; ask for a room close to the dining area if mobility is a concern.

name: Hotel Barahi
summary: A long-running hotel on Lakeside in Pokhara, named after the lake goddess of Tal Barahi, close to Phewa's main boat stands. A practical, comfortable mid-range base for the city, trek starts and rest days.
body: Hotel Barahi stands in the heart of Lakeside, within a few minutes' walk of Barahi Ghat, where boats leave for the island temple of Tal Barahi that gives the hotel its name. Around it are the restaurants, bakeries, trekking agencies and gear shops that make Lakeside work as a base, and the lake path for evening walks.

It is the kind of hotel many travellers use twice in one trip: before a trek to sort permits and gear, and after it for a hot shower and a lake view. Ask for an upper-floor room on the side facing the mountains, as views depend on the room. Book early for October and November.
why: Central Lakeside location near Barahi Ghat
Easy walk to agencies, cafes and boats
Reliable base before and after treks

faqs.q: Where is Hotel Barahi in Pokhara?
faqs.a: Hotel Barahi is in central Lakeside, Pokhara, a short walk from Barahi Ghat and the boats to Tal Barahi temple. Restaurants, shops, trekking agencies and the lake path are all close by. It is about 15–20 minutes by taxi from Pokhara International Airport and the Tourist Bus Park.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Barahi good for trekkers?
faqs.a: Yes. Its central Lakeside location puts trekking agencies, permit offices, gear shops and cafes within walking distance, and many trekkers use it before and after Poon Hill, Mardi Himal or Annapurna Base Camp. Ask about storing extra luggage while you trek; most Lakeside hotels can do this.

faqs.q: Can you see Phewa Lake from Hotel Barahi?
faqs.a: The hotel is very close to the lake, and some upper-floor rooms and terraces have partial views of Phewa and, on clear days, the mountains. Views vary by room, so ask for a mountain or lake-facing room when booking. The lakeshore path is a minute or two's walk away.

name: The Old Inn
image_query: The Old Inn Bandipur Newari house
summary: A heritage inn in two carefully restored Newar townhouses on Bandipur's car-free main street, keeping original wooden doorways and red brick. Rooms over three floors face the mountains or the bazaar, with a dining room opening onto the street and a quieter back terrace.
body: The Old Inn occupies two old merchant houses in the middle of Bandipur's bazaar, said to be around 150 and 250 years old, restored to keep their Newar character: carved wooden doorways, exposed red brick, low ceilings and steep stairs. Rooms vary in size and style across three floors, all with en suite bathrooms, furnished with local textiles. Some look to the Himalaya, others over the street.

Meals mix Nepali and continental cooking. You can eat in the dining room that opens onto the bazaar, watching the town go by, or on the terrace at the back with valley views and more privacy. Staying here puts you on the street at dusk and dawn, Bandipur's best hours, with Thani Mai and Tundikhel a short walk away.
why: Restored Newar townhouses on the car-free bazaar
Rooms with Himalaya or street views

faqs.q: Where is The Old Inn in Bandipur?
faqs.a: The Old Inn is on Bandipur's main bazaar street, in the middle of the car-free old town. Vehicles park at the edge of the bazaar, a few minutes' walk away; staff can help with bags. From the inn, Tundikhel and the path to Thani Mai hill are short walks.

faqs.q: What are the rooms like at The Old Inn?
faqs.a: Rooms are spread over three floors of two restored Newar townhouses, varying in size and style, all with en suite bathrooms and traditional furnishings. Some face the mountains, others the bazaar. Expect character, low doorways and steep wooden stairs rather than modern hotel space. Ask for a mountain-view room when booking.

faqs.q: Is The Old Inn suitable for older travellers?
faqs.a: It is popular with older travellers who enjoy heritage buildings, but the restored houses have steep, narrow stairs and low doorways, and some rooms are on upper floors. Mention mobility needs when booking so the inn can offer a lower room. The flat, car-free bazaar outside is easy to walk.
